verdict.rationale: Lambda's 1-Click Clusters let users launch 16–512 H100/B200 GPU clusters "instantly" with "no long-term commitments". Reservation is self-serve from the Lambda Cloud console, and the docs specify GPUDirect RDMA at up to 3200 Gb/s plus InfiniBand-enabled managed Kubernetes and Slurm for multi-node jobs. The "contact us" path applies only to discounted reserved capacity, not to cluster access. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that cluster launch is truly sales-free, and documentation of any minimum reservation duration or capacity-availability limits for 1CC.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can provision a multi-node GPU cluster with fast interconnect for distributed training without a sales cycle

citations.quote: Launch 16x to 512x NVIDIA H100 or B200 GPU clusters instantly, or start with a single-node instance. No long-term commitments.
enabling peer-to-peer GPUDirect RDMA at up to 3200 Gb/s
Navigate to the 1-Click Clusters page in the Lambda Cloud console and click Reserve 1-Click Cluster.
MK8s provides a Kubernetes environment with GPU and InfiniBand (RDMA) support, and shared persistent storage across all nodes in a 1CC.
The quick start takes you from SSH to your first multi-node GPU job in minutes.
